problem: Existing VLN agents such as DUET, HAMT and RecBERT pick the next node by matching candidates to 2D panoramic subviews. Because of the adjacency rule, several candidate nodes can map to the same subview, which makes action selection ambiguous. Panoramic features also discard 3D scene layout, occluded objects and object geometry, so the agent struggles to ground spatial references such as 'the chair furthest from the front door'.
motivation: Bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception from autonomous driving turns multi-view images into a metric top-down grid that keeps spatial layout and object geometry, and it serves both perception and planning. Candidate nodes that share one panoramic subview fall into different BEV grid cells, so BEV gives a discriminative decision space. 3D detection supervision can make that representation object-aware, which suits the object-centric instructions in REVERIE and R2R.
key_idea: Build an online topological graph whose node embeddings come from local BEV grid features learned under 3D oriented-box detection supervision. Then fuse a graph-level score, a BEV grid-level score (Gaussian-pooled onto candidate nodes) and DUET's panoramic scores to choose the next viewpoint.
insight: BEV geometry complements panoramic features rather than replacing them. On REVERIE val-unseen the BEV branch alone is worse than the DUET base (SR 39.03 vs 46.98), but combined with it reaches 52.12 (Table 4). The 3D detection supervision is what makes the BEV features useful: removing it drops REVERIE SR from 52.12 to 49.25 and R2R SPL from 62.33 to 60.20, and navigation tracks detector quality (mAP LSS 0.188 → BEVDepth 0.252 → BEVFormer 0.299 gives REVERIE SR 50.83 → 51.06 → 52.12). Supervising with oriented rather than axis-aligned boxes raises REVERIE SR from 49.25 to 52.12. Smaller gains come from each remaining component: temporal BEV updating (50.30 → 52.12), using both graph and grid decision spaces (50.18 graph-only or 48.25 grid-only vs 52.12), a 9-grid node neighborhood over 4 or 16, and Gaussian over uniform pooling (51.27 vs 52.12; the table's checkmark layout for this row is ambiguous).
method: View transformation (BEVFormer-style voxel sampling): the 6 raw horizontal Matterport3D camera images (1280×1024, ImageNet ViT-B/16 features, known intrinsics/extrinsics) are queried by predefined 3D reference points via cross-attention. The grid is 11×11 BEV queries over a [-5 m, 5 m] x/y range, with Z=4 height anchors in [-1 m, 2 m]. Voxel pooling then gives a BEV map B_t of D-dim grid features.

Matterport3D² amodal 3D detection pretraining: a new dataset of oriented 3D bounding boxes for 17 indoor categories, derived by PCA over object segments. Objects count as visible if their center projects inside the camera frustum; there are 92,221 train boxes over 3,463 viewpoints, using the VLN train/val/test splits. The BEV encoder plus a DETR-style head (bipartite matching, focal loss + L1) is trained separately from the policy.

BSG construction: each current or candidate node embedding is the average of its 9 nearest BEV grid features. Grid features in the overlap between B_t and B_{t+1} are temporally updated by cross-attention, and nodes observed multiple times get averaged embeddings. A hallucinated 'stop' node is added.

Graph-level decision score: an LXMERT-initialized cross-modal encoder (9 text layers, 2/4 cross-modal layers) runs over the node embeddings and instruction words. An FFN then gives scores over all N_t+1 graph nodes (the global action space, as in DUET).

Grid-level decision score: a second cross-modal transformer over the 121 BEV grids and the instruction produces a score per grid cell. A truncated bivariate Gaussian (μ=0, diagonal σ=2) pools these cell scores into scores for each local candidate node.

Score fusion: local candidate scores are mapped to global space through backtracking (summing scores along visited nodes to reach unconnected nodes). They are fused with the graph score using W_f=0.5, and the BSG branch is then combined with DUET's panoramic branch (weights 0.7 / 0.3).

Training: pretraining uses MLM, MRC (panoramic branch only), SAP with progress monitoring for the BEV branch, and OG for REVERIE (batch 32, 100k iterations, 4×RTX 3090). Fine-tuning uses teacher-forcing plus student-forcing with a pseudo-interactive (DAgger-style) expert, adds the OG loss on REVERIE (α=0.20), and runs at lr 1e-5, batch 8, 25k iterations.

setting.backbone: DUET-based dual-branch cross-modal transformer (LXMERT-initialized) plus a BEVFormer BEV encoder on ImageNet ViT-B/16 features; the BEV encoder is trained separately with 3D detection supervision
setting.training_data: Pretraining and fine-tuning use R2R, R4R and REVERIE train splits plus the same speaker-synthesized instructions as DUET. The BEV encoder is pretrained on the authors' Matterport3D² 3D detection dataset: oriented boxes for 17 categories from Matterport3D segments, 3,463 train viewpoints, 92,221 boxes.
setting.observation: Multi-view RGB (6 raw horizontal Matterport3D camera images with calibrated intrinsics/extrinsics) for the BEV branch, 36-view panoramic RGB for the DUET panoramic branch, and candidate object features on REVERIE. No depth input is used by the default BEVFormer model.
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (global graph action space with backtracking + stop)
setting.privileged: None beyond the standard discrete-VLN setup: nav-graph candidate positions, used to locate node neighborhoods in the BEV grid; camera calibration of the raw Matterport images; and REVERIE's provided candidate object boxes.

numbers_note: The main R2R table prints integer SR and SPL. The ablation tables give the full model on R2R val-unseen as SR 73.73 and SPL 62.33, and the base DUET as 71.52 / 60.36. Results for BEV scale and perception range appear only in a figure (Fig. 5). Detection results on Matterport3D² are reported separately and are not navigation benchmarks: val unseen mAP 0.299 / mAR 0.488 at IoU 0.5; test unseen AP50 0.295 / AR50 0.485 (Table 9).
results: On REVERIE val-unseen, BSG beats its base DUET: SR 52.12 vs 46.98, SPL 35.59 vs 33.73, RGS 35.36 vs 32.15. On REVERIE test-unseen it reaches SR 56.45 vs DUET's 52.51, though its RGSPL of 22.34 is slightly below LANA's 22.85 despite the paper's bolding. On R2R test-unseen it improves DUET from SR 69 to 73, SPL 59 to 62 and NE 3.65 to 3.19, but with a longer TL (14.86). On R4R val-unseen it gets SR 47 vs HAMT's 45 and nDTW 53, while CLS 59 trails LANA's 60 and NE 6.12 trails HAMT's 6.09.
limitations: The BEV detector and navigation policy are trained separately, not end-to-end. The approach needs raw calibrated Matterport camera images rather than simulator panoramas, plus custom 3D box annotations, which ties it to Matterport3D and the discrete nav-graph.
Accuracy on flat or small objects is poor: picture AP50 is 0.053 and lighting 0.103. The BEV range is fixed at 10 m × 10 m with an 11×11 grid, and the chosen scale and range depend on room structure.

Evaluation covers only static simulated environments with discrete viewpoints; no continuous-environment or real-robot results are given. Trajectories also get longer than DUET's (e.g., REVERIE val-unseen TL 24.71 vs 22.11).
